clue.text: Get to drop in

explanation.definitionFit: To come by something is to acquire it, and to come by someone's house is to visit casually.

clue.text: Present time in which misc. trash gets distributed!

indicators.note: the letters of misc. trash are scattered and dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: The festive season when assorted rubbish ends up everywhere, wrapping paper and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present time' is a time for presents, not the here and now.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the season of giving gifts, hence a time for presents.

clue.text: Left in distress, giving little away

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left sits inside the word for unhappiness

parts.note: misery is great unhappiness

explanation.surface: Someone left in a sorry state who reveals little.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person is stingy and reluctant to spend or give anything.

clue.text: Inferior pottery in Glos. estate

parts.note: bad means of poor quality
Minton is a famous Staffordshire pottery and its china

explanation.surface: Second-rate ceramics found on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Glos. is Gloucestershire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a ducal estate in Gloucestershire, home of the famous horse trials.

clue.text: Schemes to get US soldier, terribly sick, to collect award for fighting

indicators.note: the soldier and the jumbled letters gather up the medal between them

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American private soldier

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word sick is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: A tale of an American serviceman, unwell, picking up a medal for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'award for fighting' is the Military Medal, which the soldier and ICKS ('terribly' sick) hold between them, as 'to collect' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimmicks are tricks or ploys devised to attract attention, a sense close to schemes.

clue.text: Iran isn't getting new arrangement with bloke being bloody-minded

indicators.note: the words Iran isn't are given a fresh ordering of their letters

parts.note: gent is an informal word for a man

explanation.surface: A political headline about a nation stubbornly refusing a new deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting new arrangement' turns IRANISNT into INTRANSI.
explanation.definitionFit: An intransigent person stubbornly refuses to compromise, which is what being bloody-minded means in British usage.

clue.text: Food to satisfy, from what we hear

indicators.note: this signals that a word is being spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: Talk of food that is said to fill you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat is animal flesh eaten as food, and loosely any food, as in 'meat and drink'.

clue.text: Money wasted at once, very little saved

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the small piece safe inside them
wasted suggests the words at once are ruined and reshaped
only a little of the word very is kept, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Cash frittered away at a stroke, with hardly anything kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' turns ATONCE into CENTAO; 'saved' places V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A centavo is a small coin, a hundredth of the peso in several Latin American countries.

clue.text: Old-fashioned means of transport for one upwardly mobile

definitions.text: Old-fashioned means of transport for one upwardly mobile

parts.words: Old-fashioned means of transport for one upwardly mobile
parts.note: an enclosed chair carried on poles by two bearers, lifting one well-to-do passenger off the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' usually means socially climbing; here the passenger is literally lifted up and moved about.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was a covered seat for one person, carried on poles in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Live with soldiers, having joined team

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Someone moving in with the army after signing up to a squad.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there.

clue.text: Not relaxed, having gone through a screening process

definitions.text: having gone through a screening process
definitions.meaning: passed through a sieve or filter

explanation.definitionFit: Strained means tense or forced, and also describes liquid passed through a sieve.

clue.text: The star grins, disguising deepest feelings

indicators.note: the words the star grins are disguised by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A celebrity smiling to hide how they really feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartstrings are one's deepest emotions, as in tugging at the heartstrings.

clue.text: Member of Royal Navy maybe planting tree on isle

parts.note: the service tree is a European tree related to the rowan
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A sailor busy with tree planting on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor in the Royal Navy is one example of someone serving in the armed forces.

clue.text: Big building, pub with name at the back

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is placed behind the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place

explanation.surface: A large pub with its sign on the rear wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a large farm building used for storing grain or housing animals.

clue.text: Time getting degree — years!

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
Y is the usual abbreviation for year or years

explanation.surface: A student lamenting how long their degree has taken.
explanation.definitionFit: May is a month, a period of time on the calendar.

clue.text: Priest dancing before job — inspired by this female?

indicators.note: the word priest is set dancing, its letters jigging into a new order

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A clergyman hoofing it before getting on with his duties, prompted by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns PRIEST into TERPSI. Terpsichore is the Greek Muse of dance, so the dancing priest is fittingly inspired by her.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muse is a goddess who inspires artists; this one presides over dance.

clue.text: Jazz fan, the chap going round Ireland to see girl

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

indicators.note: the pronoun for a man encircles the poetic name

parts.note: he refers to a man
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A jazz lover travelling around Ireland to visit a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: They praise those no longer in the belfry team?

parts.note: ex means former
bell ringers who toll the bells are tollers

explanation.surface: Retired bell ringers singing praises.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as EX-TOLLERS means former bell ringers.
explanation.definitionFit: Extollers are people who praise something highly.

clue.text: Not the first place said to show unusual perception?

parts.note: second is the position after first

indicators.note: said means the word for place is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: A runner-up claiming a strange gift of insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Second sight is the supposed power to perceive future or distant events, a paranormal ability.

clue.text: Language of particular group in a Spanish bar

parts.note: cant is jargon or slang peculiar to a group

explanation.surface: Jargon from a certain crowd heard in a Spanish drinking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a bar or tavern in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Club attraction, one to be avoided

indicators.note: the numeral is left out of the lure

parts.note: bait is a lure that attracts
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nightclub's draw that people would rather steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat is the wooden implement used to strike the ball in cricket or baseball, a kind of club.

clue.text: Wave from demolition worker

definitions.meaning: a large wave crashing on the shore
someone who smashes things up, such as a wrecker

explanation.definitionFit: A breaker is a heavy wave that breaks on the shore, and also someone who breaks things up.

clue.text: Enthusiastic supporters or cooler types?

definitions.meaning: devoted followers of a team or star
devices that cool, playfully put as if they were people

explanation.definitionFit: Fans are devotees of a team or performer, and also electric or hand-held devices for cooling air.

clue.text: Female stars making appearances

parts.note: aces are experts or stars at something

explanation.surface: Actresses turning up on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in appearances is to show one's face, so faces fits appearances.

clue.text: One grape munched by the Spanish — bit of fruit often discarded

indicators.note: chewing the words one grape breaks them up into a new order

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A Spaniard snacking on a grape, while some fruit waste is thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'munched' makes ORANGEPE from 'One grape'; 'the Spanish' is the Spanish word for 'the', not a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange peel is the rind of a citrus fruit, usually thrown away after peeling.

clue.text: You and I will get record and express emotion

parts.note: we stands for you and I together
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Two people recording a song that makes them emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to cry, shedding tears as a show of feeling.

clue.text: Prominent features around grassland for South Americans

indicators.note: the facial features enclose the meadow

parts.note: chins are features of the face that can jut out
a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

explanation.surface: Striking landmarks surrounding a stretch of open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Chileans are the people of Chile, a South American nation.

clue.text: Pet left half abandoned after short while

indicators.note: the half word follows the moment

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

indicators.note: only the first half of the word left is kept, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: A pet deserted and left alone after a brief spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet and to tickle are both ways of stroking or touching someone playfully.

clue.text: Lively holiday complex exists — keep quiet about it!

indicators.note: the call for silence is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
a camp, such as a holiday camp, is a site of holiday chalets
is means exists

explanation.surface: A rowdy holiday resort being told to hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampish describes the playful, mischievous liveliness of a young rascal.

clue.text: Finds out little initially, then gets paid

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of little

parts.note: to earn is to receive payment for work

explanation.surface: Someone who discovers little at first but then gets a salary.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to discover or come to know it.
